posts.name: Aman Kumar
posts.cooked:
In Quiz 1 Pyq Session, it said that in this question screenshot pasted below we have to keep in mind that error word will at once only in a line, My question is that it can be Error01 or Error: or multiple Error words in a line

image810×607 61 KB

How do we know that we have to suppose what in these questions

posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked:
Yes, you are correct.

If you want to count number of lines that have “ERROR”, options (a) and (d) are correct.

grep -c ERROR filename

and

grep ERROR filename | wc -l

However if you want to count the number of occurences (counting multiples occurences per line as well) we should do:

grep -o ERROR filename | wc -l

This works because -o will print only the match and each match on separate lines, which then is passed to wc to count the number of lines in output, which is same as the number of matches.

Aman_Kumar:

Similarly there was also a question about string matching but in that there was not grep command so it was told that we have to suppose this thing if there is grep then only we have to consider using ‘’ escape character else it will be wrong

Your framing is very ambiguous, I would recommend pasting the question here so we can understand your doubt and guide you.

Regards,
Sayan

posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked:
If the question only requires to count lines, then they are correct.

In the absence of a competing option, (a) and (d) are the most (and equally) correct options. Usually when in doubt, choose the most correct options.

However I agree the clarification should be present whether to count lines or occurences.

posts.name: Aman Kumar
posts.cooked:
Sir it is written in question

count the number of occurrences of the word "ERROR" in the file

Related to this I want to ask one more thing

What if it asks

count the number of occurrences of the string "ERROR" in the file

Then if the file contains Error or Error: or Error230, do we have to count all those occurrences as it is said to be string not a word. As word is a combination of letters separated with spaces.

posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked:
Aman_Kumar:

Sir it is written in question

count the number of occurrences of the word "ERROR" in the file

If this is present in the question explicitly then yes, the options are incorrect.
It should be grep -o ERROR filename | wc -l to do the same.

Aman_Kumar:

Related to this I want to ask one more thing

What if it asks

count the number of occurrences of the string "ERROR" in the file

Then if the file contains Error or Error: or Error230, do we have to count all those occurrences as it is said to be string not a word. As word is a combination of letters separated with spaces.

You are correct, a word is a sequence of word characters (\w) surrounded by word boundary (\b). So ideally when asked to match a word we should either use -w flag with grep, or manually surround the search with \b on both sides or \< and \> on left and right. However for string or pattern, this would not be required.

However, in most cases, the evaluator might have just meant string when saying word. Again, use the same principle, when in doubt mark the most correct option. If there are options with and without \b or -w, and they ask to match word, then choose the one with -w or \b. However if there is only one valid option and it does not have \b or -w, then choose that anyway.
